r: First to come to Hanamkonda; attacked **Kanchi (1051)** for **Someshwara I**
Made Anumakonda capital; Garuda → Varaha; **Kesari Samudram**
Saiva, initiated by **Rameswara Pandita** of Srisailam
**Victory pillar at Srisailam**; killed by the **Velanati Chodas**; Yadava conflict began
Invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva; died on an elephant crossing a river

2.x: **Rudradeva's wars:** defeated the Kalachuri confederacy (Mailagi, Medaraja, Dommaraja) in **1159**, the **Telugu Chodas** and **Tailapa III**; his accession is recorded in the **Draksharama** inscription (1158) of the minister Inangala Brahmi Reddi.

r: **Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya** ("founder of the Kakati Rajya"), Raya Pitamahanka

2.x: **Ramappa (Rudreswara) temple** = **Kakatiya**; **UNESCO World Heritage Site 2021**; **floating bricks**; star-shaped platform.

r: Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya; source for Prolaraja's history
Independence; Prola II's conquests; composed by **Achitendru**, found by **J.S. Fleet**
Beta I first king; Durga Nripathi's accession

4.x: **June 2026:** an ASI survey of the **Nallamala** copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records of the 2nd–16th c.

r: Conflict began under **Prola II**; **Jaitugi** killed Rudradeva and held Ganapati; Mahadeva died in the revenge war; Rudramadevi repulsed the Yadava Mahadeva
Veera Ballala II's advance made Jaitugi free Ganapati; Prataparudra's commander **Pedarudru** beat **Ballala III** after 1316
**Malik Kafur** besieged Warangal in **1310** (tributary); **1323** fall; Prataparudra **died jumping into the Narmada** (Musunuri record)

5.x: **Legacy:** one tradition makes **Harihara and Bukka** treasury officers of **Prataparudra II** who fled to **Kampili** after 1323; the **Nayankara system** was carried on by Vijayanagara.

r: The **Rashtrakutas** – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta"; early emblem **Garuda**
Feudatories of the **Kalyani (Western) Chalukyas** – emblem **Varaha** (changed by **Prola I**); title **Mahamandaleswara**, borne by Beta II
Only issued the Magallu grant; never Kakatiya overlords
Samanta (feudatory) 956–1162 → **sovereign 1163–1323**; the Kakatiyas ruled Andhra in the **12th–13th centuries**

0.x: Founding dates: Hoysalas 10th–11th c., Gahadavalas 11th c., Kakatiyas and Yadavas 12th c.

r: **First mention** of the Kakatiyas – Kakatiya **Gundyana** (Kakara Gundana)
Best genealogy; line begins with **Venna (Venna Bhupati)**
Names **Beta I** as the **first Kakatiya king**; records the accession of **Durga Nripathi**

0.x: **Early base:** **Hanamkonda (Anumakonda) Vishaya**, received by Beta I through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.

r: **Rameswara Pandita** (Mallikarjuna matha, **Srisailam**) → **Beta II**; **Dhruveshwara Pandita** → **Mahadeva**; **Visvesvara Sivacharya** (Golaki Matha) → **Ganapatideva**
**Second dynasty after the Satavahanas** to unite all Telugu lands; "gave a comprehensive form to Andhraism" – the **ultimate design to Andhra culture**
Ruled by the **Kakatiyas** in the 12th–14th c.; the Seunas held the west

0.x: **P.V. Parabrahma Sastry:** **Kannada (Chalukya) rule in Andhra ended** with the establishment of the Kakatiya kingdom.

r: Developed Hanamkonda; Swayambhu temple in Orugallu
**Completed the fort** and **transferred the capital** from Hanumakonda to **Orugallu**; called it **Andhranagari**

1.x: **Ganapatideva** shifted the capital; the Bekkallu inscription (1195) already calls Orugallu **Rudradeva**'s capital, so the shift is also credited to Rudradeva.

r: **Begun by Rudradeva**, completed by Ganapatideva, strengthened by Rudramadevi
Warangal best reflects the Kakatiya contribution to culture – fort, Thousand Pillar temple, Ramappa nearby
**1199–1262** (about **63 years**, the longest); first inscription **Manthena, 26 Dec 1199**
Held captive by Yadava **Jaitugi**; **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him
Brought **the whole Telugu area under one rule** after the Satavahanas, from Ganjam to Kanchi
The most powerful Kakatiya – **extended the empire up to Kanchi**
Coastal campaign – general **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**; married **Narama and Perama**, daughters of **Pinnachodi**; made their brother **Jayapa** **Gajasahani**
With **Choda Tikka** of Nellore killed **Prithviswara** → Velanati kingdom ended (title **Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda**)
With Akkana and Bayyana killed **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** – final end of the Velanati Chodas
Restored **Manumasiddhi II** after the poet **Tikkana** came as envoy; Tikkana dedicated **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to **Manumasiddhi**
Fought the **Eastern Gangas** for southern Kalinga and Vengi
**Jatavarman Sundara Pandya** beat the Kakatiyas at **Muttukur** (Nellore); **Nellore fell to the Pandyas**

3.x: The **Pithapuram inscription** of Velanati **Prithvisvara** names **Kolleru Lake**.

r: **Ramappa temple** (Recherla Rudra, 1213), **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks, **Ganapavaram** villages, **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (1244)
**Telugu replaced Sanskrit** in inscriptions from his reign
Succeeded him, raised as a son (putrika), trained by her mother **Kupama Devi**; married **Veerabhadra** of the **Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukyas**
**Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married the sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**

3.x: Rudrama defeated the Pandyas, Eastern Gangas and Seunas; Marco Polo visited Motupalli ("Mutfili") in her reign.
**Ganapatideva**, the greatest Kakatiya, largely restored the **political unity of the Telugu country**.
